name: Swivel joint
function: A joint with two or three rotating elbows on ball-race bearings that lets a treating line absorb misalignment and movement between the missile, manifold, and tree.

tabs.overview: Two-piece swivels give one axis of rotation; three-piece give three. Long-sweep elbows reduce erosion compared with short-radius ones. Bearings are grease-packed and the seal is a replaceable packing.
tabs.engineering: Rated with the iron; swivels are the most erosion-prone item in a treating line because the flow turns inside them.
tabs.safety: Swivels are inspected for wall loss at the elbows and for play in the bearings; a swivel that leaks at the packing is removed from service, not tightened under pressure.
tabs.evidence: API 6A (S1) for pressure-containing parts and connections; public OEM pages (S2, S3, S5, S11, S12) for configurations; field and manufacturing practice (S9).

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
Tree saver in the wellhead; valves fully open or fully closed only; iron inspection.
